_comment: An entry belongs here only when a platform package is CORRECT to carry a
string literal equal to a route some registered language declares as its
readiness or liveness probe -- i.e. the literal is NOT an application probe
target at all (an infrastructure container's own probe, a gateway
framework-path list). An application probe is never exempted: it reads
Each entry pins the file AND the exact matched line, so it cannot widen into
a whole-file allowance; an entry whose line no longer exists fails the gate.
expected_count must equal the number of entries: remediation removes the entry
and decrements the count in the same change.

exemptions.reason: Loki's own readiness endpoint: a probe for an infrastructure container the docker platform provisions, whose route is Loki's, not a generated application's. gateway_routes.py records that infra-container probes are owned by the provisioning platform.

The compose healthcheck for the Loki infrastructure container, probing Loki's own /ready endpoint. Infrastructure-container probe owned by the provisioning platform; no generated application is behind it.

The raw-socket readiness probe for the Promtail infrastructure container (its image ships no HTTP client), targeting Promtail's own /ready endpoint. Infrastructure-container probe owned by the provisioning platform.

Module docstring of the emitted ZITADEL test JWKS fixture server, describing the /health route the same file mounts below. The template IS the server that mounts the route, so the literal is the route's definition, not a platform assumption about a language's application.

The emitted ZITADEL test JWKS fixture server's own request router mounting its /health route. The template IS the server; the literal defines the route rather than assuming one on a generated application's behalf.

_NGINX_INFRA_EXCLUDE_PATHS: the fixed set of framework-owned gateway paths that bypass JWT auth on the nginx side. It is an auth-exemption list, not a probe target; the per-service public health route the gateway forwards is minted by gateway_routes from the service's declared health_check.path.
